title: 16-06-pace-code-c-2015.pdf — section 34
text:
6.6 If paragraph 6.5(b)(i) applies, once sufficient information has been
obtained to avert the risk, questioning must cease until the
detainee has received legal advice unless paragraph 6.5(a), (b)(ii),
(c) or (d) applies.

6.7 A detainee who has been permitted to consult a solicitor shall be
entitled on request to have the solicitor present when they are
interviewed unless one of the exceptions in paragraph 6.5 applies.

6.8 The solicitor may only be required to leave the interview if their
conduct is such that the interviewer is unable properly to put
questions to the suspect. See Notes 6C and 6D.

6.9 If the interviewer considers a solicitor is acting in such a way, they
will stop the interview and consult an officer not below
superintendent rank, if one is readily available, and otherwise an
officer not below inspector rank not connected with the
investigation. After speaking to the solicitor, the officer
consulted will decide if the interview should continue in the
presence of that solicitor. If they decide it should not, the suspect
will be given the opportunity to consult another solicitor before
 27
the interview continues and that solicitor given an opportunity to
be present at the interview. See Note 6D.
